verdict.rationale: DBOS's core is an open-source library that runs inside your own program, with Postgres as its only infrastructure dependency. That makes it inherently self-hosted, and the public GitHub repo plus co-founder statements corroborate this. Docs also say Conductor and the DBOS Console can be self-hosted, for example via Docker Compose. Older community comments that the observability web UI was not open source or self-hostable concern the console, not the core library. missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation of self-hosted Conductor/Console, clarity on licensing of the self-hosted management UI

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: The open-source DBOS library uses Postgres to orchestrate durable workflows and queues. There's no separate orchestration server and no infrastructure required besides Postgres.
DBOS is an open-source Postgres-backed library. To add DBOS to an application, you install the open-source library and annotate workflows and steps.
you can self-host Conductor and the DBOS Console on your development machine using Docker Compose.
DBOS runs as a library inside your program
